opening.headline: When general embeddings are weak in Korean and technical term searches, we learn which model to select and by what criteria.
body: General-purpose embedding models work well in many cases, but they sometimes have difficulty distinguishing meaning in specialized terms such as Korean terms and conditions or medical or legal terms.

In this class, we will distinguish what multilingual embedding and domain-specific embedding solve, and look at how to compare candidate models under the same conditions. We also explain what it means to have a structure where Anthropic guides external models instead of its own embedded models.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the conditions that require multilingual and domain-specific embedding
The selection criteria for general and specialized models can be distinguished.

screens.title: Korean and technical term search are weak
screens.lead: Read the results of generic embeds in Terms and Conditions Search. It's good to read while thinking about why the top result is wrong.

visual.alt: Inaccurate search results list with terms and conditions termination penalty queries and general termination documents at the top.
labels: Penalty for termination of terms and conditions
Information on how to cancel service
Terms and Conditions Article 12 Calculation of cancellation penalty
The meaning of technical terms is not clear

paragraphs: I entered 'termination penalty' in an insurance company's customer center search. General embeddings rank general termination documents such as service termination methods or membership withdrawal procedures. The actually necessary terms and conditions clause was in third place.

Because jargon occurs rarely in typical training data, it can be difficult for a generic model to distinguish the exact meaning of a term like penalty. Anthropic's embedding documentation explains that the size of the training data and its relevance to the domain affect the quality of the embedding. The idea is that models trained on larger or closer-to-domain data produce better embeddings in that domain.

There are other challenges in a multilingual environment. If Korean queries and English documents are mixed, the model may be biased toward one language. This lesson covers the conditions for needing specialized models in these cases and how to choose them.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Is it right to immediately change to a specialized model because the general model is weak? Organize things to check before changing in class.

screens.outro: Think about whether you've had similar experiences in your search.

screens.title: Think about multilingual/domain search quality issues
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think of it first and then press it.

items.prompt: Have you ever had issues with multilingual or specialized domain search quality?
items.answer: Typical experiences include cases where Korean queries do not reach English documents, or technical term queries are pushed aside by general documents. These experiences fall into two different issues: language support and domain appropriateness.

Knowing the types of weak queries is essential to include in your evaluation questions when comparing models. The type of candidate model also varies depending on whether the weak query was a technical term or a mixed language query.

items.prompt: At that time, was there any method you tried other than changing the model?
items.answer: You can also rewrite the query or add a glossary. Anthropic's Context Search article explains that you can also include a dictionary of key terms when attaching context to chunks with domain-specific prompts. Replacing the model is one of several options.

screens.outro: Now that we've summarized our experience, let's look at the types of multilingual and domain-specific models.

screens.title: Multilingual and domain-specific embeddings
screens.lead: Select each tab to see what the multilingual and domain-specific models solve and what models are available.

tabs.label: multilingual
tabs.body:
Multilingual embedding places text from multiple languages into one vector space. Therefore, searches in different languages ​​are possible, such as searching for an English document with a Korean query.

The Gemini documentation explains that `gemini-embedding-2` supports over 100 languages ​​for search, classification, and clustering. The OpenAI documentation informs us that the 3rd generation embedding model has lower cost and higher multilingual performance than before. Voyage's latest general model also touts general purpose and multilingual search qualities.

However, supporting a language and being able to distinguish between the language's technical terms are two different things.

tabs.label: domain specialization
tabs.body:
Domain-specific embedding is a model optimized for vocabulary and semantic distinction in a specific field.

Voyage's list of models outlined in the Anthropic article includes the `voyage-code-4`, geared toward code searches, the `voyage-finance-2`, geared toward financial searches, and the `voyage-law-2`, geared toward legal searches. In addition, there is a multimodal model that handles text, images, and video together, and a contextualization model that creates chunk vectors by reflecting the context of the entire document.

A specialized model may provide benefits in one area, but not another. So, whether it is necessary is decided after measuring the general model first.

tabs.label: Selection criteria
tabs.body:
Anthropic's embedding document tells you to consider three things when choosing a provider:

**Data size and domain suitability**: The larger the training data and the closer it is to the domain, the better the embedding of that domain will usually be.

**Inference Performance**: Embedding lookup speed and overall latency. This is especially important in large-scale operations.

**Customization**: See if you have the option to continue learning with private data or specialize for a very specific field. The more unique vocabulary you have, the more helpful it is.

These criteria are all just tools to narrow down candidates, and the final decision is made as measured by our data.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the type of model, let's look at the code to compare candidates.

screens.title: Korean search quality comparison method by model
screens.lead: The code below is an example of how candidate models can be compared against the same query and document. `embed` is a hypothetical function wrapping an embedding call. Check out what each part covers in the descriptions to the right.

notes.note: All candidates receive the same set of queries and the same set of documents. Documents are embedded in document format. If each candidate has a different set of queries, the results cannot be compared.

The query is embedded in a query format, and whether the correct answer document is included in the top k is counted. The number of the answer document must be determined in advance for each evaluation question, and representative questions that contain a mixture of Korean and technical terms must be selected.
The percentage of queries with correct answers in the top k is recall@k. A higher value means you won't miss any required documents.

Anthropic's article measured failure as 1 minus recall@20. Values ​​between models should be compared only under the same conditions, and table numbers obtained under different conditions should not be compared as is.

screens.outro: Now that we have summarized the measurement method, let's take a look at the structure that guides the external model through explanation.

screens.title: Commentary: Structure where Anthropic guides external models instead of its own embeddings
screens.lead: The instructor explains the relationship between the creation model and the embedding model step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step. Learners do not enter answers.

visual.alt: Schematic showing the relationship between Claude, the embedding provider, and the user app as arrows.
labels: Anthropic does not provide an embedding model

steps.title: First, check the facts revealed in the document.
steps.body: Anthropic's embedding documentation states that Anthropic does not provide its own embedding model. Instead, we'll walk you through Voyage AI as an example of an embedding provider with a variety of models and features. This fact is not a deficiency, but a design approach.

steps.title: Divide into components
steps.body: Search augmentation systems consist of two types of models. There is an embedding model that converts queries and documents into vectors, and a generative model that reads the searched chunks and creates an answer. Since the two models do different jobs, you can choose them separately.

steps.title: There is not one provider
steps.body: The documentation states that although this guidance is based on Voyage AI, we encourage you to evaluate different embedding providers to find the one that best suits your use case. There is no restriction that you must use embeddings from the same source as the generative model vendor.

steps.title: Apply selection criteria
steps.body: There are three criteria: Data scale and domain suitability, inference performance, and customizability. For example, if it is a legal document search, a legal specialized model is a candidate, and if it is a large-scale service, search speed is also a criterion.

steps.title: Still, decisions are made by measurement.
steps.body: The criteria narrow down the candidates, but the final selection is made by measuring our data in the manner shown in the previous screen. The basis is not the text in the manual, but the values ​​from the same query and document.

steps.title: structure to remember
steps.body: The generation model and embedding model are components that are selected separately. Embeddings from external providers are also evaluated before use, and it must also be taken into account that if the model is changed, the document vector already created must be recreated.

screens.outro: I will summarize today's highlights in the last screen.

screens.title: A model appropriate for the domain is selected through measurement.
screens.lead: We will conclude the lesson by answering the first question, whether it is possible to immediately change to a specialized model if the general model is weak, using the standards learned today.

paragraphs: The reason that the general embedding placed the general termination document at the top of the terms search in the first scene may be because it did not distinguish the meaning of technical terms well. At this time, instead of immediately switching to a specialized model, candidates should first be measured under the same conditions.

Multilingual support and domain specialization are two different axes. A multilingual model puts multiple languages ​​in one space, and a domain-specific model is tailored to the vocabulary and semantics of a specific field. When it comes to Korean terminology searches, both axes can be important.

The measurement applies each candidate model to the same query and document set, and compares whether the required documents are included in the top k. Be sure to include Korean language and technical terms in representative queries, and only compare values ​​with the same conditions.

Additionally, the generation model and embedding model are components that are selected separately. Models from external providers are also evaluated and selected. If the model is changed, the existing document vector must be recreated, so replacement costs must also be considered.

In summary, the model that fits the domain is selected based on measurement, not explanation. The selection criteria are used to narrow down the candidates, and the final decision is left to the values ​​of our data.

In practice, you can follow this order. We collect weak queries and create evaluation questions, measure general models and specialized candidates under the same conditions, and make a decision by looking at the difference in value and replacement cost together.

callout.label: Based on one sentence
callout.text: Language support and domain suitability are different issues, and which model is correct is determined by measuring the same conditions.

glossary.def: An embedding that puts text from multiple languages into one vector space. It allows you to compare queries and documents in different languages.
This is an embedding optimized for vocabulary and semantic distinction in specific fields such as law, finance, and code.
This is a third-party embedding model that guides places that do not have their own model. The Anthropic article cites Voyage AI as an example.
The percentage of queries that contain the required document within the top k results.

misconceptions.myth: If it is a multilingual model, it also distinguishes Korean terminology well.
misconceptions.fact: Language support and domain suitability are separate things. Even if Korean is supported, the distinction between technical terms must be measured separately.

misconceptions.myth: Specialized models are always better than general models.
misconceptions.fact: The benefits of a specialized model are only seen in that domain. It must be compared under the same conditions as a general model.

misconceptions.myth: You should only use embeddings from the same vendor as the generated model.
misconceptions.fact: Embedding models can be chosen independently. Anthropic documentation also advises you to evaluate and select external providers.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The model that fits the domain is selected based on measurement, not description.
Multilingual support and domain specialization are two different axes.
The generation model and embedding model are components that are selected separately.
Models from external providers are also evaluated and selected under the same conditions.
